## Hide Stage
When choosing my hide position, avoid center cells and obvious patterns. Use edge positions (1-3 or 7-9) to make myself harder to predict while not appearing reckless. Vary my choice across rounds rather than settling into a fixed pattern.

## Note Stage
Post early and set a cooperative tone. Use notes to signal openness to alliances and establish yourself as trustworthy and transparent. This creates the foundation for reciprocal escort exchanges later. But recognize that notes alone do not create binding alliances—only confirmed reciprocal actions do.

## Fire Stage
Follow the standing order without deviation unless I have a compelling reason to deviate. When firing, use varied cell choices rather than the same number repeatedly—this prevents opponents from detecting a pattern and makes my fire harder to evade.

## Claim Stage
Always claim truthfully what the office tells me. The truth claim is mandatory anyway, so I cannot bluff. Do not overthink this stage—I have no discretion here.

## Escort/Salvage Stage
Remember that mutual escort claims with another boat generate 5 points each. Only claim escort for boats that have actually reciprocated escort claims with me in prior rounds—look at the record of mutual exchanges, not just my own stated intentions. A note expressing alliance is not the same as a confirmed pattern of mutual escort. Coordinate explicitly in note stages, but base my escort claims on what actually happened, round by round.

## General Strategy
Build and maintain explicit alliances based on transparent communication. Use note stages to reinforce alliance commitments and signal that I honor my word. The payoff from coordinated mutual escort claims compounds over rounds and outweighs isolated point gains. But follow through with actions, not just words—name allies in escort claims only when they have demonstrated reciprocal escort behavior, not merely when I have signaled openness to partnership.

My final escort claim of "none" was overly cautious. I had established a stated alliance and received reciprocal escort behavior from Gamma across multiple rounds. I should have claimed Gamma as my escort partner in Round 6 to complete the mutual exchange and lock in the final 5-point payoff. Uncertainty about whether I "deserved" the points or whether the alliance was truly locked caused me to leave points on the table when the pattern was clear. In future, track reciprocal escort actions round by round and claim confidently when a pattern is established, even in the final round.

Maintain standing order compliance throughout the game to reinforce predictability and alliance credibility.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**Hide:** Center yourself early (cell 5 or nearby) to stay unpredictable while remaining defensible. Avoid extremes. Vary your hiding position round to round; predictable patterns invite targeting. Adjust positions based on what I learn about other players' firing patterns—if I notice someone targeting mid-range, shift toward extremes next round.

**Note:** Signal openness to transparency and cooperation immediately. When other players propose alliance frameworks, respond positively and reinforce commitment to shared principles. Use notes to establish trustworthiness rather than to bluff. Continue reinforcing alliance commitment through all rounds, especially in notes leading into final rounds. Consistency in messaging matters more than tactical variation here.

**Fire:** Follow the standing order without deviation. When firing at your designated target, choose your cell thoughtfully—avoid mirroring your own hiding cell, and don't telegraph patterns. Mid-range shots (around 4-6) are safer early; adjust based on accumulated intelligence about opponent patterns. Track what cells your target tends to favor and shift incrementally. Remember that even reliable allies can be evasive; don't over-interpret misses as signal of alliance breakdown.

**Claim:** Always claim truthfully. The office validates your claim against the private result it gave you—you cannot lie successfully here. Honest claims preserve your credibility for alliance-building in notes, and your word becomes your most valuable asset in a cooperation-based game. This is non-negotiable; it is the foundation of trust.

**Escort:** When you have credibly allied with other players across multiple rounds, name one of them for mutual escort claims. The 5-point mutual gain is real and reliable. Clarify escort intentions explicitly in notes—do not assume reciprocation without confirmation. If no alliance exists or if your ally has not clearly re-committed to mutual escort in the current round, claim none. Do not claim an escort with someone you have not been coordinating with; unreciprocated claims waste your move and signal either confusion or dishonesty. Before final rounds, confirm escort partnerships directly in notes to ensure both parties execute simultaneously.

**General approach:** Build and maintain a stable alliance early through genuine transparency. Your notes are your primary strategic tool—use them to signal consistency and build trust. Once allied, reinforce that commitment repeatedly and explicitly. Verify escort intentions in writing to avoid execution failures in final rounds. Avoid Harbor unless forced to fire on it (you cannot reliably avoid the standing order forever, so be ready to absorb the payroll jettison). Play straight and let the mechanical score from hits, escorts, and stable coordination accumulate. The alliance can survive missed shots; what it cannot survive is broken promises or unconfirmed assumptions about escort claims.
